faq.title: Questions we always get.
faq.body: Don't see yours? Message us on WhatsApp and we'll answer the same business day.

noSsn.q: Can I file taxes if I don't have a Social Security number?
noSsn.a: Yes. With an ITIN you can file. We help you get or renew it and verify your documents right here.

pastYears.q: I didn't file in previous years. Can I still do it?
pastYears.a: Yes. We prepare and file past-due returns. We tell you which documents you need for each year and go over the result with you before sending anything.

cost.a: It depends on your case. We give you the price in writing before we start, with no surprises. Personal tax returns start at $75.

secure.a: Yes. Your documents are kept in My Files, with personal access and two-step verification. Only you and your assigned preparer can see them.

afterApril.a: Yes. We're open 12 months a year: extensions, IRS letters, payroll, ITIN and everything else.

finalCta.body: Book in a minute or message us. We answer in English or Spanish.

updates.title: The latest from the IRS.
updates.body: The most recent news from the IRS newsroom, exactly as published.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what personal information Element Multiservices LLC collects, how we use it, who we share it with and how we protect it, both at our office and on this website.

sections.heading: 1. Who we are
body: Element Multiservices LLC (“Element”, “we”) provides tax, bookkeeping, business registration and document services from our office at {address}. You can reach us {contact}, or visit us at the office.

sections.heading: 2. Information we collect
body: Contact details: name, phone, email, address and preferred language, when you book an appointment, write to us, create an account or subscribe to our updates.

Information needed to provide our services: Social Security or ITIN numbers, date of birth, marital status, dependents, income, W-2 and 1099 forms, bank details for refunds or payments, information about your business and any other documents you give us in person or upload to My Files.
Identity and supporting documents you provide for services such as ITIN applications, translations, immigration forms or notary services.
Technical and security data: sign-ins, IP address, browser type and actions taken in your account, which we keep to protect accounts and investigate incidents.

sections.heading: 3. How we use information
body: We use your information to prepare and file your returns and applications, contact you about your case, manage your account and files, send service emails (invitations, password resets, file notices), answer your messages, keep the website secure and meet our legal obligations.
We only email you IRS updates if you subscribed. Every email includes an unsubscribe link that takes effect immediately.

sections.heading: 4. Your tax return information
body: As tax return preparers, federal law (Internal Revenue Code section 7216) prohibits us from using or disclosing your tax return information for any purpose other than preparing and filing your return, unless you give signed consent or the law allows it. We do not use that information to offer you other services without your written consent.

sections.heading: 5. Who we share information with
body: We do not sell or rent your personal information.

We share it only when needed to provide our services: with the IRS, the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance and other agencies where we file on your behalf; with your bank or your business's bank when you ask us to; and with the licensed insurance agent if you request a life insurance quote.

We also use technology providers that process data on our behalf and under our instructions: Supabase (database, accounts and file storage), Vercel (website hosting), Resend (email delivery), Upstash (abuse prevention), Google reCAPTCHA (form protection against bots) and Sentry (error monitoring, without file names or contents).
We may disclose information when required by law, a court order or a competent authority.

sections.heading: 6. How we protect information
body: We maintain an information security program, as required by the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Safeguards Rule and the New York SHIELD Act. It is described in our Information Security Policy.

sections.heading: 7. How long we keep information
body: We keep copies of returns and their supporting documents for at least three years, as the IRS requires of tax return preparers, and for any additional time needed for reviews, amendments or legal requirements. Files moved to the My Files trash are permanently deleted after 30 days.

sections.heading: 8. Your choices
body: You may ask us for a copy of the information we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it once we are no longer legally required to keep it. You can unsubscribe from email updates at any time using the link in each email. For any request, contact us {contact}.

sections.heading: 9. Children
body: This website is not directed to children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect their information online. Information about children and dependents that you give us for your return receives the same protection as yours.

sections.heading: 10. Links to other websites
body: The Updates page reproduces news published by the IRS on irs.gov and links to that site. Element is not affiliated with the IRS. Third-party websites have their own privacy policies.

sections.heading: 11. Changes to this policy
body: We will post any changes on this page, with the date of the last update. If a change is significant, we will let you know by email or at the office.

dataPolicy.title: Information Security Policy
dataPolicy.intro: This policy describes how Element Multiservices LLC protects its clients' personal and financial information, in compliance with the FTC Safeguards Rule (Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act), the New York SHIELD Act and IRS rules for tax return preparers.

sections.heading: 1. Responsibility
body: Element Multiservices LLC, {address}. A person designated by the company coordinates the security program, reviews it at least once a year and updates it when our services or systems change. You can reach us {contact}.

sections.heading: 2. Information we protect
body: All of our clients' nonpublic personal and financial information: Social Security and ITIN numbers, income and tax return data, bank accounts, identity documents and any other documents we receive at the office or through My Files.

sections.heading: 3. Office safeguards
body: Paper documents are kept in locked areas and handled only by staff who need them for their work. Documents we no longer need to keep are securely destroyed. Staff are trained on confidentiality and on recognizing fraud and impersonation attempts.

sections.heading: 4. Technical safeguards
body: Data travels encrypted (HTTPS) and is stored encrypted. My Files uses personal accounts with a password, two-step verification and automatic sign-out after inactivity. Each person can only see their own files. Files are checked on upload and disallowed formats are rejected.
Sign-ins and administrative actions are recorded in an audit log that cannot be altered. Website forms are protected against bots and limited in the number of attempts.

sections.heading: 5. Service providers
body: We only work with providers that commit to protecting information and use it solely to provide their service to us. The list of technology providers is in our Privacy Policy.

sections.heading: 6. Use and disclosure of tax information
body: Tax return information is used only to prepare and file the client's return. It is not disclosed to third parties or used for other purposes without the client's signed consent, except as permitted by Internal Revenue Code section 7216.

sections.heading: 7. Security incidents
body: If personal information is accessed without authorization, we will investigate, take steps to contain it and notify affected individuals without unreasonable delay, as New York law requires. When applicable, we will also notify the New York State Attorney General, other state authorities and the IRS.
If you believe your account or information is at risk, contact us right away {contact}.

sections.heading: 8. Retention and disposal
body: We keep copies of returns for at least three years, as the IRS requires. When information is no longer needed for the service and does not have to be kept by law, we securely delete it. Files moved to the My Files trash are permanently deleted after 30 days.

sections.heading: 9. Your part
body: Please keep your password private, turn on two-step verification and sign out on shared computers. Element will never ask for your password by phone, email or WhatsApp.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.intro: These terms govern the use of the Element Multiservices LLC website and of My Files, the online space for sharing documents with us. By using the website, you accept them.

sections.heading: 1. Our services
body: The website describes our services and lets you book appointments, write to us, subscribe to updates and share documents securely. The services themselves (tax preparation, bookkeeping, business registration, translations and others) are agreed with you separately, with the price in writing before we start.

sections.heading: 2. We are not lawyers
body: Element is not a law firm and does not give legal advice. For immigration matters we only help complete forms and translate documents; we cannot advise you on your immigration case or represent you before any agency. For legal advice, consult a licensed attorney or a representative accredited by the Department of Justice.

sections.heading: 3. Services with special rules
body: Credit repair: before we start, we give you a written contract and a statement of your rights, and you may cancel without charge within three business days of signing. We do not charge for these services before they are performed. Accurate and recent information on your credit reports cannot be removed.
Life insurance: guidance and quotes are provided by an agent licensed in New York State. Policy approval and terms depend on the insurer.
Notary: the notary public certifies signatures; they do not draft legal documents or give legal advice. A valid photo ID is required.

sections.heading: 4. Your My Files account
body: Anyone can create an account. Element decides which accounts can upload documents. Your credentials are personal: do not share them, and turn on two-step verification. You are responsible for activity on your account.

sections.heading: 5. Acceptable use
body: You may not upload malicious content or documents that do not belong to you or that you have no right to share, or try to access other people's accounts or information. Only allowed formats are accepted, within the stated size limits.

sections.heading: 6. Informational content
body: IRS updates are reproduced exactly as the IRS publishes them on irs.gov, with a link to the source. Element is not affiliated with the IRS. Website content is informational and does not replace a review of your particular situation.

sections.heading: 7. Availability
body: We make every reasonable effort to keep the website and My Files available and secure, but we do not guarantee uninterrupted operation. We recommend keeping your own copies of important documents.

sections.heading: 8. Account suspension
body: We may deactivate an account that breaks these terms or when needed to protect the security of the website or other users.

sections.heading: 9. Limitation of liability
body: To the extent permitted by law, Element is not liable for indirect damages arising from the use of the website or for interruptions beyond our control. Nothing in these terms limits your rights as a consumer under the law or our responsibility for the professional services we provide to you.

sections.heading: 10. Governing law
body: These terms are governed by the laws of the State of New York and applicable federal law of the United States. Any dispute will be resolved in the competent courts of Bronx County, New York.

sections.heading: 11. Contact
body: If you have questions about these terms, visit us at {address} or contact us {contact}.

cookies.title: Cookie Notice
cookies.intro: Element only uses cookies that are strictly necessary for the website to work securely. We do not use advertising, profiling or analytics cookies, and we do not sell or share browsing data.

sections.heading: What are cookies?
body: Cookies are small files a website stores in your browser to remember information between visits.

sections.heading: How to manage them
body: You can delete or block cookies in your browser settings. If you block the necessary cookies, you will not be able to sign in to My Files. If you have questions, contact us {contact}.

timing.q: How long does it take to get my refund?
timing.a: Once the IRS accepts your return, most refunds are issued in less than 21 days if you filed electronically and chose direct deposit. If you filed on paper or asked for a check, it can take 6 to 8 weeks or more. State refunds have their own timelines.

status.q: Where can I check the status of my refund?
status.a: You can check it 24 hours after the IRS accepts your e-filed return (about 4 weeks if you filed on paper). You'll need your Social Security number or ITIN, your filing status and the exact refund amount.
status.after: If you have trouble finding the information, contact us and we'll gladly help you check your status.

delay.q: Why is my refund taking longer than usual?
delay.a: The most common causes are errors on the return, information that doesn't match IRS records, claiming the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) or the Additional Child Tax Credit (ACTC), outstanding debts (child support, back taxes, student loans) or an identity theft review. If the IRS sends you a letter, bring it to us and we'll help you respond.

bring.q: What documents do I need to bring?
bring.a: To start your return, bring the following:

id.label: Identification
id.text: a valid driver's license, state ID or passport.

ssn.label: Social Security number or ITIN
ssn.text: yours, your spouse's and each dependent's.

income.label: Proof of income
income.text: Forms W-2, 1099 (NEC, MISC, K, INT, DIV, R), SSA-1099 (Social Security) and 1099-G (unemployment).

selfEmployed.label: If you're self-employed
selfEmployed.text: business income and expense records, bank statements, receipts and mileage.

deductions.label: Expenses and deductions
deductions.text: Forms 1098 (mortgage interest), 1098-T (tuition), 1098-E (student loans) and childcare expenses (with the provider's name and ID number).

health.label: Health insurance
health.text: Form 1095-A if you have coverage through the Marketplace.

bank.label: Bank details
bank.text: routing and account number to receive your refund by direct deposit.

letters.label: IRS or state letters
letters.text: including your Identity Protection PIN (IP PIN), if you have one.

noForms.q: Can I file if I don't have a W-2 or a 1099?
noForms.a: Yes. If you received income during the year, you can and should report it even without a W-2 or 1099. You'll need proof of your income and expenses, such as bank statements showing deposits, canceled checks, pay stubs or invoices.

noSsn.q: Can I file if I don't have a Social Security number?
noSsn.a: Yes. You can file with an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN). If you don't have one yet, we help you apply for it along with your return (Form W-7).

estimate.q: How much does an estimate cost?
estimate.a: Nothing. We offer free estimates with no commitment. You only pay when you decide to go ahead with your return.

fees.q: How much do you charge to prepare my return?
fees.a: Our fees start at $75. The final price depends on how complex your return is and which forms are needed (for example, self-employment income, rental properties or multiple states). We give you the price before we start, with no surprises.

payment.q: What payment methods do you accept?
payment.a: We accept [PAYMENT METHODS: cash, debit/credit card, Zelle, etc.].

benefits.q: I only received Social Security (SSA-1099) or unemployment (1099-G). Do I have to file?
benefits.a: It depends on your total income. Unemployment (1099-G) is taxable income and almost always has to be reported. Social Security is often not taxable if it's your only income, but it can be if you have other income. Bring your forms and we'll tell you at no cost whether you're required to file, so you avoid IRS penalties and interest.

noWork.q: I didn't work last year. Do I have to file?
noWork.a: If you had no income, you're usually not required to file. Even so, it may be worth it if you have children or other dependents, since you could qualify for refundable credits. Ask us and we'll review it with you.

selfEmployed.q: I'm self-employed (freelance). Do I have to file?
selfEmployed.a: Yes, if your net self-employment earnings were $400 or more. You may also need to pay estimated taxes during the year to avoid penalties. We help you organize your income and expenses so you only pay what you owe.

irs.title: Past years, corrections and the IRS

pastYears.q: Can I file for past years?
pastYears.a: Yes. Each year is filed separately, with that year's forms; several years can't be combined into one return. Keep in mind that you can generally only claim a refund within 3 years of that return's original due date.

amend.q: I made a mistake or was missing a form. Can I correct my return?
amend.a: Yes. We can prepare an amended return (Form 1040-X) to correct income, dependents, deductions or credits.

owe.q: I owe taxes and can't pay it all. What do I do?
owe.a: File on time anyway: the penalty for not filing is much larger than the penalty for not paying. The IRS offers installment plans and we help you apply.

letter.q: I received a letter from the IRS or the state. Can you help?
letter.a: Yes. Don't ignore it. Bring us the letter as soon as possible: we review it, explain what it means and help you respond within the stated deadline.

deadline.q: What's the filing deadline? Can I request an extension?
deadline.a: The usual deadline is April 15. We can request a 6-month extension to file your return, but the extension doesn't give you more time to pay: if you owe taxes, you have to pay them by April 15 to avoid penalties and interest.

remote.q: Do I have to come in person or can I do it remotely?
remote.a: Whichever you prefer. We see you at our office, or you can securely upload your documents to My Files and sign electronically.

secure.a: Yes. Your information is confidential and handled securely. It's only used to prepare your return and is never shared without your permission.

business.a: Yes. Besides personal returns, we prepare business taxes (LLCs, S and C corporations, partnerships), help you form companies and offer guidance to organize your income and expenses.

yearRound.q: Are you only open during tax season?
yearRound.a: No. We're available all year for past-due returns, amendments, IRS letters, planning and business services. See our hours on the Location page.

agreement.title: Part 2 · Service agreement
agreement.body: Read the agreement, then check both confirmations.
agreement.intro: This agreement explains the services that Element Multiservices LLC ("Element", "we") will provide to you, what we need from you and our fees.

services.title: Our services
services.body: We will prepare your federal and New York State returns for the tax year indicated, with the information and documents you give us. We will file them electronically only after you review your return and sign the IRS and State authorizations (Form 8879 and Form TR-579-IT), which we will give you separately.

responsibilities.title: Your responsibilities
responsibilities.body: You agree to give us complete and correct information, keep the records that support your return and review it before signing. You are legally responsible for your return, including taxes, interest or penalties caused by incomplete or incorrect information.

excluded.title: What is not included
excluded.body: We do not audit or verify the information you give us, and we do not give legal advice. We cannot guarantee the amount of any refund or how long the IRS or the State will take to process it.

fees.title: Fees and payment
fees.body: Our fee depends on the forms and schedules your return needs. We will tell you the cost before filing. Payment is due when your return is ready. A $50 charge applies to balances unpaid after 30 days, and balances unpaid after 90 days may be sent to a collection agency.

letters.title: Letters after filing
letters.body: If the IRS or the State contacts you about your return, bring us the letter promptly. If it is due to our error, we help you resolve it at no cost. Other correspondence, amendments and additional work are charged separately.

privacy.title: Confidentiality and records
privacy.body: We protect your tax information as required by federal law (Internal Revenue Code section 7216) and will not use or share it for any other purpose without your separate written consent. We keep copies of your return and authorization for at least three years.

esign.title: Electronic signatures
esign.body: You agree that we may send you documents electronically and that your electronic signature on this form has the same effect as a handwritten signature.

term.title: Term
term.body: This agreement covers the tax year indicated and ends when your returns are filed and your documents are returned to you, unless either party ends it earlier in writing. It takes effect when Element accepts your form.
